title: Thy Glory, Holy Three in One
description: Thy Glory, Holy Three in One in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 1 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 105, “Father of angels and of men, Savior, who hast us bought, Spirit by whom we're born again, And sanctified and taught!”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy glo-ry, ho-ly Three in One, Thy peo-ple's song shall be, Long as the wheels of time shall run, And to e-ter-ni-ty.

lines: Thy glory, holy Three in One,
Long as the wheels of time shall run,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
